# webhooks.cc full reference

> Webhook testing tools for developers. Capture, inspect, forward, and test webhooks with a dashboard, CLI, TypeScript SDK, and MCP server for AI agents.

## What is webhooks.cc?

webhooks.cc is a webhook inspection and testing service. Developers use it to capture incoming HTTP requests at unique URLs, inspect headers and bodies in real time, configure mock responses with conditional rules (route different responses based on method, path, headers, body, or query params), forward webhooks to localhost for local development, and write automated test assertions against captured requests.

Every endpoint on an account also receives email at `<slug>@mailhooks.cc`. Captured emails sit in the same request list as webhooks and can be forwarded to your own server as signed JSON.

The Rust receiver handles 86,000+ requests per second with sub-millisecond capture latency. Requests are written directly to Postgres via a single stored procedure and surfaced in the dashboard through Supabase Realtime.

## Architecture

- **Dashboard**: Next.js App Router with real-time updates via Supabase Realtime Broadcast signals (database triggers send id-only signals on private topics; the dashboard then re-reads through authenticated API routes)
- **Receiver**: Rust (Axum + Tokio) writing directly to Postgres via sqlx and a single stored procedure
- **Email intake**: a receive-only Rust SMTP host for `mailhooks.cc` that hands each message to the receiver, which stores it through the same stored procedure as webhooks
- **Email forwarding**: a queue drained by the web app, which signs and posts each captured email to the endpoint's forwarding URL
- **Database**: Self-hosted Supabase (Postgres) with row-level security
- **CLI**: Rust (Clap + Ratatui) connecting via SSE streams
- **SDK**: TypeScript (`@webhooks-cc/sdk`) published to npm
- **MCP Server**: TypeScript (`@webhooks-cc/mcp`) for AI coding agents

## URLs

- Homepage: https://webhooks.cc
- Webhook receiver: https://go.webhooks.cc
- Endpoint URL format: `https://go.webhooks.cc/w/<slug>` or `https://go.webhooks.cc/w/<slug>/optional/path`
- Endpoint email address format: `<slug>@mailhooks.cc` or `<slug>+<tag>@mailhooks.cc`
- Documentation: https://webhooks.cc/docs
- Email capture: https://webhooks.cc/docs/email-capture
- Email forwarding: https://webhooks.cc/docs/forwarding
- REST API: https://webhooks.cc/docs/api
- OpenAPI spec: https://webhooks.cc/openapi.yaml
- Installation: https://webhooks.cc/installation
- GitHub: https://github.com/kroqdotdev/webhooks-cc
- npm SDK: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@webhooks-cc/sdk
- npm MCP: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@webhooks-cc/mcp

## Pricing

- **Guest** (no signup): 25 requests per ephemeral endpoint, deleted after 12 hours, no email capture
- **Free**: 50 requests per 24 hours, unlimited endpoints, 7-day retention, every feature including email capture and full CLI/SDK/MCP access
- **Pro** ($8/month): 100,000 requests per 30 days, 31-day retention
- **Teams** ($12/seat/month): a separate per-team subscription, not a tier of a personal plan. Each seat adds 100,000 requests per 30 days to a pooled team quota and one member slot. Requests on endpoints shared with an active team are billed to the pool and kept 31 days.
- Emails count against the same quota as webhooks: one request per email per endpoint it is addressed to.

## Authentication

API keys use the `whcc_` prefix. Generate from https://webhooks.cc/account or via `whk auth login`.

Protected endpoints require a Bearer token:
```
Authorization: Bearer whcc_...
```

Public (unauthenticated) routes: `POST /api/auth/device-code`, `POST /api/auth/device-token`, `POST /api/go/endpoint`.

---

## TypeScript SDK Reference

Package: `@webhooks-cc/sdk` on npm.

### Installation

```bash
npm install @webhooks-cc/sdk
```

### Client Constructor

```typescript
import { WebhooksCC } from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";

const client = new WebhooksCC({
  apiKey: "whcc_...",         // Required
  baseUrl: "https://webhooks.cc",         // Optional
  webhookUrl: "https://go.webhooks.cc",   // Optional
  timeout: 30000,             // Request timeout in ms
  retry: {                    // Optional retry policy
    maxAttempts: 3,
    backoffMs: 1000,
    retryOn: [502, 503, 504],
  },
  hooks: {                    // Optional lifecycle hooks
    onRequest: (info) => {},
    onResponse: (info) => {},
    onError: (info) => {},
  },
  emailDomain: "mailhooks.cc", // Optional, the domain emails.address() uses
});
```

### Endpoints

```typescript
// Create endpoint
const endpoint = await client.endpoints.create({
  name?: string,              // Display name
  ephemeral?: boolean,        // Auto-expire
  expiresIn?: number | string,  // e.g. "12h"
  mockResponse?: MockResponse,
  responseRules?: ResponseRule[],  // Conditional response rules (first match wins)
  notificationUrl?: string,   // Slack/Discord URL
});
// Returns: Endpoint { id, slug, name, url, createdAt, ... }

// List all endpoints
const endpoints = await client.endpoints.list();
// Returns: Endpoint[]

// Get single endpoint
const ep = await client.endpoints.get("my-slug");

// Update endpoint
const updated = await client.endpoints.update("my-slug", {
  name?: string,
  mockResponse?: MockResponse | null,  // null clears mock
  responseRules?: ResponseRule[] | null,  // null clears all rules
  notificationUrl?: string | null,     // null clears notification
});

// Delete endpoint
await client.endpoints.delete("my-slug");

// Send test webhook to your own endpoint
const response = await client.endpoints.send("my-slug", {
  method?: string,            // Default: "POST"
  headers?: Record<string, string>,
  body?: unknown,             // JSON-serialized if object
});

// Send provider webhook template
await client.endpoints.sendTemplate("my-slug", {
  provider: "stripe",        // stripe|github|shopify|twilio|slack|paddle|linear|sendgrid|clerk|discord|vercel|gitlab|typeform|standard-webhooks|meta|lemonsqueezy|coinbase-commerce|razorpay|cal|intercom|telegram|square|hubspot|mailgun|calendly|mux|sentry|bitbucket|docusign|adyen|paypal|plaid|resend|workos
  template?: string,         // Provider-specific preset
  secret: "whsec_test",      // Template signing input (omit for unsigned templates: sendgrid|discord|plaid)
  event?: string,            // Event type override
  timestamp?: number,        // For deterministic signatures
});
```

### Requests

```typescript
// List recent requests
const requests = await client.requests.list("my-slug", {
  limit?: number,
  since?: number,           // Timestamp in ms
  kind?: "http" | "email",  // Only HTTP requests or only emails
});

// Paginated listing
const page = await client.requests.listPaginated("my-slug", {
  limit?: number,
  cursor?: string,          // From previous page
  kind?: "http" | "email",
});
// Returns: { items: Request[], cursor?: string, hasMore: boolean }

// Get single request (emails have kind: "email" and the parsed message in `email`)
const req = await client.requests.get("request-id");

// Wait for next request (polling)
const req = await client.requests.waitFor("my-slug", {
  timeout?: number | string,     // Default: "30s", e.g. "5m"
  pollInterval?: number | string, // Default: "500ms"
  match?: (request: Request) => boolean,
  since?: number,                 // Default: five minutes ago, so a request that just arrived is found
});

// Wait for multiple requests
const reqs = await client.requests.waitForAll("my-slug", {
  count: 3,
  timeout?: number | string,
  match?: (request: Request) => boolean,
});

// Stream requests in real time (SSE)
for await (const req of client.requests.subscribe("my-slug", {
  signal?: AbortSignal,
  timeout?: number | string,
  reconnect?: boolean,
  maxReconnectAttempts?: number,  // Default: 5
})) {
  console.log(req.kind, req.method, req.path);  // streamed requests carry kind, not the parsed email
}

// Replay captured request to a URL (throws for emails)
const response = await client.requests.replay("request-id", "http://localhost:8080");

// Search requests
const results = await client.requests.search({
  slug?: string,
  method?: string,
  kind?: "http" | "email",
  q?: string,               // Free-text search
  from?: number | string,   // Start time
  to?: number | string,     // End time
  limit?: number,           // Default: 50
  offset?: number,
  order?: "asc" | "desc",
});

// Count matching requests
const count = await client.requests.count({ slug: "my-slug", method: "POST" });

// Clear requests
await client.requests.clear("my-slug", { before?: number | string });

// Export requests (HTTP only; emails are skipped)
const exported = await client.requests.export("my-slug", {
  format: "har" | "curl",
  limit?: number,
  since?: number,
});
```

### Emails

Every endpoint on an account receives email at `<slug>@mailhooks.cc` and `<slug>+<tag>@mailhooks.cc`; guest endpoints receive none. A captured email is a request with `kind: "email"`, `method: "EMAIL"`, the recipient address as `path`, the raw message as `body` and the parsed message as `email` (typed `EmailRequest`). An email counts as one request.

```typescript
import { extractCode, extractLink, extractFromEmail } from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";

// The address, optionally with a +tag (pass the Endpoint object to use its emailAddress)
const address = client.emails.address("my-slug", "run-42"); // "my-slug+run-42@mailhooks.cc"

// Criteria shared by list, latest, waitFor, waitForAll (all given criteria must match):
//   tag?: string | null        exact, case-sensitive; null = untagged mail only
//   subject?: string | RegExp  string = substring
//   from?: string | RegExp     string = address, case-insensitive; RegExp tested against "Name <address>"
//   to?: string | RegExp       To, Cc, or the address it was delivered to; same rules as from

// List emails, newest first (limit = newest emails fetched before filtering, default 50)
const emails = await client.emails.list("my-slug", { tag: "run-42", limit: 50, since: Date.now() - 60_000 });

// One email by request ID (NotFoundError if the request is not an email)
const one = await client.emails.get("request-id");

// The newest matching email among the 100 newest, or null
const latest = await client.emails.latest("my-slug", { subject: "Confirm" });

// Poll until a matching email arrives; throws TimeoutError
const email = await client.emails.waitFor("my-slug", {
  tag: "run-42",
  timeout: "60s",            // Default: 60000
  pollInterval: "1s",        // Default: 1000
  since: Date.now(),         // Default: five minutes ago
  match: (e) => e.email.attachments.length === 0,  // Extra filter
});

// Poll until `count` matching emails arrive, oldest first
const several = await client.emails.waitForAll("my-slug", { count: 2, tag: "run-42" });

// Deliver a sample email with a 6-digit code and a link (counts as one request, no SMTP, no sender checks)
const sent = await client.emails.sendTest("my-slug", { tag: "run-42" });
// Returns: { status: "captured", requestId: string | null }

// The email.received JSON forwarding would post (no API call)
const event = client.emails.toJson(email, {
  endpoint: { slug: "my-slug", name: "Signup flow" },  // Optional; fills data.endpoint.name
  includeExtracts: true,                                // Default: true (codes and links)
});

// Code and link finder (no API call); accepts a request or the parsed email
extractCode(email);                          // "482913" or null
extractLink(email);                          // action link (confirm, verify, reset, sign in), else the first link worth keeping
extractLink(email, { actionOnly: true });    // only an action link, or null
extractFromEmail(email.email);               // { codes: string[], links: { url, label, action }[] }
```

`@webhooks-cc/sdk/email` exports the email types (`EmailCapture`, `EmailReceivedEvent`, ...), `extractCode`, `extractLink`, `extractFromEmail`, `htmlToText`, `buildEmailJson`, `emailAddress` and `isValidEmailTag`, with no network code (browser-safe).

`requests.replay()` throws for emails, `requests.export()` skips them, and provider detection ignores them. Requests from `requests.subscribe()` carry `kind` but not `email`; call `client.emails.get(id)` for the parsed message.

### Forwarding

Owner only: for anyone else these throw `NotFoundError` (`configure` fails with 403 for team members).

```typescript
// Set the URL and/or turn forwarding on or off; returns the Endpoint.
// The first URL creates the signing secret. url: null removes it (forwarding must be off).
await client.forwarding.configure("my-slug", { url: "https://example.com/hooks/email", enabled: true });

// The whsec_ signing secret (NotFoundError before a URL was saved)
const secret = await client.forwarding.secret("my-slug");

// Replace the secret; every delivery from now on, retries included, uses the new one
const rotated = await client.forwarding.rotateSecret("my-slug");

// Post the newest email (or a sample) to the URL once; works with forwarding on or off
const result = await client.forwarding.test("my-slug");
// Returns: { status: number | null, durationMs, excerpt: string | null, error: string | null, delivered: boolean, sample: boolean }

// The endpoint's latest deliveries, newest first (limit 1-20, default 5)
const recent = await client.forwarding.deliveries("my-slug", { limit: 10 });
// Returns: RecentEmailDelivery[] { id, requestId, status, attempts, createdAt, lastStatus, lastError, subject }

// Every delivery of one email, with each try in attemptLog
const deliveries = await client.forwarding.emailDeliveries("request-id");
// Returns: EmailDelivery[] (see Delivery under Email Forwarding below)

// Queue the email again with the current URL and secret (409 when forwarding is off)
const { id } = await client.forwarding.redeliver("request-id");
```

Verify a forwarded email in your handler. `verifyForwardedEmail` checks `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` (within `toleranceSeconds`, default 300) and `webhook-signature` against the raw body and the `whsec_` secret, then parses the body as an `email.received` event:

```typescript
import { verifyForwardedEmail, WebhookVerificationError } from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  try {
    const event = await verifyForwardedEmail(
      await request.text(),       // raw body: string, Uint8Array (Buffer) or ArrayBuffer
      request.headers,            // Fetch Headers, a plain object (Node/Express req.headers) or [name, value] pairs
      process.env.FORWARD_SECRET!,
      { toleranceSeconds: 300 }   // Optional; also `now` (ms) for tests
    );
    console.log(event.data.subject, event.data.codes);
    return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof WebhookVerificationError) {
      // error.code: "missing_headers" | "timestamp_out_of_range" | "invalid_signature" | "invalid_payload"
      return new Response(error.message, { status: error.code === "invalid_payload" ? 400 : 401 });
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

Test a handler locally without forwarding: `sendTo` with the `standard-webhooks` provider signs the body with the given secret and sends `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature`, which `verifyForwardedEmail` accepts (the `webhook-id` is random rather than derived from the email's id):

```typescript
await client.sendTo("http://localhost:3000/hooks/email", {
  provider: "standard-webhooks",
  secret: process.env.FORWARD_SECRET!,
  body: client.emails.toJson(email),
});
```

### Send to Arbitrary URLs

```typescript
// Send webhook to any URL (not just your endpoints)
const response = await client.sendTo("https://example.com/webhook", {
  method?: string,
  headers?: Record<string, string>,
  body?: unknown,
  provider?: string,        // For signed payloads
  secret?: string,
  event?: string,
});

// Preview without sending
const preview = await client.buildRequest("https://example.com/webhook", { ... });
// Returns: { url, method, headers, body }
```

### Usage

```typescript
const usage = await client.usage();
// Returns: { used, limit, remaining, plan: "free"|"pro", periodEnd }
```

### Matchers

All matchers return `(request: Request) => boolean` for use with `waitFor` and `waitForAll`:

```typescript
import {
  matchMethod,      // matchMethod("POST")
  matchHeader,      // matchHeader("stripe-signature") or matchHeader("content-type", "application/json")
  matchPath,        // matchPath("/api/**"), glob wildcards
  matchQueryParam,  // matchQueryParam("token", "abc")
  matchBodyPath,    // matchBodyPath("data.object.id", "cs_123"), dot-notation
  matchBodySubset,  // matchBodySubset({ type: "checkout.session.completed" })
  matchContentType, // matchContentType("application/json")
  matchAll,         // matchAll(matchMethod("POST"), matchHeader("stripe-signature"))
  matchAny,         // matchAny(matchMethod("POST"), matchMethod("PUT"))
  matchEmail,       // matchEmail({ tag: "run-42", subject: "Confirm" }), same criteria as client.emails
  isEmailRequest,   // isEmailRequest(request): type guard for a captured email with its parsed message
} from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";
```

### Provider Detection Helpers

```typescript
import {
  isStripeWebhook,     // Checks stripe-signature header
  isGitHubWebhook,     // Checks x-github-event header
  isShopifyWebhook,    // Checks x-shopify-hmac-sha256 header
  isSlackWebhook,      // Checks x-slack-signature header
  isTwilioWebhook,     // Checks x-twilio-signature header
  isPaddleWebhook,     // Checks paddle-signature header
  isLinearWebhook,     // Checks linear-signature header
  isDiscordWebhook,    // Checks x-signature-ed25519 + x-signature-timestamp
  isSendGridWebhook,   // Checks body for sg_event_id
  isClerkWebhook,      // Checks svix-id header
  isVercelWebhook,     // Checks x-vercel-signature header
  isGitLabWebhook,     // Checks x-gitlab-event or x-gitlab-token header
  isStandardWebhook,   // Checks svix-id header (Polar, Svix, Clerk, Resend)
} from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";
```

### Body Parsing Helpers

```typescript
import {
  parseJsonBody,      // parseJsonBody(request) → parsed JSON or undefined
  parseFormBody,       // parseFormBody(request) → Record<string, string | string[]>
  parseBody,           // Auto-detect content-type and parse
  extractJsonField,    // extractJsonField<T>(request, "data.object.id")
  matchJsonField,      // matchJsonField("event", "invoice.paid"), returns matcher
} from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";
```

### Error Classes

```typescript
import {
  WebhooksCCError,    // Base error (statusCode, message)
  UnauthorizedError,  // 401: invalid/missing API key
  NotFoundError,      // 404: resource not found
  TimeoutError,       // Request timeout
  RateLimitError,     // 429: includes retryAfter, limit, remaining, reset
  ApiError,           // General API error
  WebhookVerificationError,  // From verifyForwardedEmail(); `code` says which check failed
} from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";
```

### Type Definitions

```typescript
interface Endpoint {
  id: string;
  slug: string;
  name?: string;
  url?: string;
  notificationUrl?: string;
  isEphemeral?: boolean;
  expiresAt?: number;       // Unix ms
  createdAt: number;        // Unix ms
  responseRules?: ResponseRule[];  // Conditional response rules
  sharedWith?: TeamShare[];
  fromTeam?: TeamShare;
  emailAddress?: string | null;  // null for guest endpoints
  showEmailExtracts?: boolean;
  forwardEnabled?: boolean;
  forwardUrl?: string | null;    // owner only
  hasForwardSecret?: boolean;
}

interface Request {
  id: string;
  endpointId: string;
  method: string;
  path: string;
  headers: Record<string, string>;
  body?: string;
  bodyRaw?: string;         // Base64-encoded raw bytes
  queryParams: Record<string, string>;
  contentType?: string;
  ip: string;
  size: number;             // Bytes
  receivedAt: number;       // Unix ms
  kind?: "http" | "email";
  email?: EmailCapture | null;  // Parsed message, for a captured email (see Email Capture)
}

interface EmailRequest extends Request {
  kind: "email";
  email: EmailCapture;
}

interface MockResponse {
  status: number;           // 100-599
  body: string;
  headers: Record<string, string>;
  delay?: number;           // 0-30000ms
}

interface UsageInfo {
  used: number;
  limit: number;
  remaining: number;
  plan: "free" | "pro";
  periodEnd: number | null;
}
```

### SDK Quick Start Example

```typescript
import { WebhooksCC, matchAll, matchMethod, matchBodyPath } from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";

const client = new WebhooksCC({ apiKey: process.env.WHK_API_KEY! });

// Create an endpoint
const endpoint = await client.endpoints.create({ name: "stripe-test" });
console.log(endpoint.url); // https://go.webhooks.cc/w/<slug>

// Send a signed Stripe webhook
await client.endpoints.sendTemplate(endpoint.slug, {
  provider: "stripe",
  secret: "whsec_test_secret",
  event: "checkout.session.completed",
});

// Wait for it
const request = await client.requests.waitFor(endpoint.slug, {
  timeout: "30s",
  match: matchAll(
    matchMethod("POST"),
    matchBodyPath("type", "checkout.session.completed"),
  ),
});

console.log(request.headers["stripe-signature"]);

// Clean up
await client.endpoints.delete(endpoint.slug);
```

## MCP Server Reference

Package: `@webhooks-cc/mcp` on npm.

### Installation

```bash
# Claude Code
claude mcp add webhooks-cc -- npx -y @webhooks-cc/mcp

# Cursor / VS Code / Windsurf
npx @webhooks-cc/mcp setup cursor
npx @webhooks-cc/mcp setup vscode
npx @webhooks-cc/mcp setup windsurf

# Codex
codex mcp add webhooks-cc -- npx -y @webhooks-cc/mcp
```

Set `WHK_API_KEY` environment variable to your API key.

### All 25 MCP Tools

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| `create_endpoint` | name?, ephemeral?, expiresIn?, mockResponse?, responseRules?, notificationUrl? | Create a new webhook endpoint |
| `list_endpoints` | (none) | List all user endpoints |
| `get_endpoint` | slug | Get endpoint details |
| `update_endpoint` | slug, name?, mockResponse?, responseRules?, notificationUrl? | Update endpoint config |
| `delete_endpoint` | slug | Delete endpoint |
| `create_endpoints` | count (1-20), namePrefix?, ephemeral?, expiresIn? | Bulk create endpoints |
| `delete_endpoints` | slugs (array, 1-100) | Bulk delete endpoints |
| `send_webhook` | slug, method?, headers?, body?, provider?, template?, event?, secret? | Send test webhook |
| `list_requests` | endpointSlug, limit (1-100), since? | List recent requests |
| `search_requests` | slug?, method?, q?, from?, to?, limit, offset, order | Search request history |
| `count_requests` | slug?, method?, q?, from?, to? | Count matching requests |
| `get_request` | requestId | Get single request |
| `wait_for_request` | endpointSlug, timeout?, pollInterval? | Wait for next request |
| `wait_for_requests` | endpointSlug, count (1-20), timeout?, pollInterval?, method? | Collect N requests |
| `replay_request` | requestId, targetUrl | Replay request to URL |
| `compare_requests` | leftRequestId, rightRequestId, ignoreHeaders? | Diff two requests |
| `extract_from_request` | requestId, jsonPaths (1-50) | Extract JSON fields |
| `verify_signature` | requestId, provider, secret?, publicKey?, url? | Verify webhook signature |
| `clear_requests` | slug, before? | Delete captured requests |
| `send_to` | url, method?, headers?, body?, provider?, template?, event?, secret? | Send to any URL |
| `preview_webhook` | url, provider?, template?, event?, secret? | Preview without sending |
| `list_provider_templates` | provider? | List providers/templates |
| `get_usage` | (none) | Get usage and quota info |
| `test_webhook_flow` | provider?, event?, secret?, mockStatus?, targetUrl?, verifySignature?, cleanup? | Full end-to-end test flow |
| `describe` | (none) | Get SDK schema introspection |

### Supported Providers for Signed Webhooks

Stripe, GitHub, Shopify, Twilio, Slack, Paddle, Linear, Clerk, Discord, Vercel, GitLab, Typeform, Standard Webhooks

Each provider signs payloads with its native algorithm (HMAC-SHA256, Ed25519, etc.) so your handler verification code works identically to production.

---

## CLI Reference

Binary: `whk`. Install via Homebrew or download from GitHub releases.

```bash
brew install kroqdotdev/tap/whk
```

### Global Flags

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--nogui` | Disable TUI mode |
| `--json` | Output as JSON |
| `--api-url <url>` | Override API URL (env: WHK_API_URL) |
| `--webhook-url <url>` | Override receiver URL (env: WHK_WEBHOOK_URL) |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |

### Commands

```bash
whk                                    # Interactive TUI dashboard

# Authentication
whk auth login                         # Browser-based device auth
whk auth status                        # Show login status
whk auth logout                        # Clear stored token

# Endpoint management
whk create [name]                      # Create endpoint
  --ephemeral / -e                     # Auto-expire
  --expires-in <duration>              # e.g. "12h"
  --mock-status <code>                 # Mock response status
  --mock-body <text>                   # Mock response body
  --mock-header KEY:VALUE              # Mock header (repeatable)

whk list                               # List endpoints
whk get <slug>                         # Get endpoint details
whk delete <slug> [--force/-f]         # Delete endpoint

whk update-endpoint <slug>             # Update endpoint
  --name <text>
  --mock-status <code>
  --mock-body <text>
  --mock-header KEY:VALUE
  --clear-mock

# Tunneling and streaming
whk tunnel <port>[/path]               # Forward webhooks to localhost
  --endpoint <slug>                    # Reuse existing endpoint
  --ephemeral / -e                     # Delete on exit
  -H, --header KEY:VALUE              # Custom forwarding headers

whk listen <slug>                      # Stream requests to terminal

# Sending and replaying
whk send <slug>                        # Send test webhook
  --method <method>
  -H, --header KEY:VALUE
  -d, --data <string|@file>

whk send-to <url>                      # Send to any URL
  --method <method>
  -H, --header KEY:VALUE
  -d, --data <string|@file>

whk replay <id>                        # Replay captured request
  --to <url>                           # Default: http://localhost:8080

# Request management
whk requests list <slug>               # List requests
  --limit <n> --since <ts> --cursor <c>

whk requests get <id>                  # Get single request
whk requests search                    # Search requests
  --slug --method -q --from --to --limit --offset --order

whk requests count                     # Count matching requests
whk requests clear <slug> [--force]    # Delete requests
whk requests export <slug>             # Export requests
  --format har|curl --limit <n> -o <file>

# Other
whk usage                              # Show quota info
whk update                             # Self-update (SHA256 verified)
whk completions <shell>                # Generate shell completions
```

Config stored at `~/.config/whk/token.json`.

---

## REST API Reference

Base URL: `https://webhooks.cc`

All endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer whcc_...` unless noted.

### Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/api/endpoints` | Bearer | List all endpoints (owned + shared) |
| POST | `/api/endpoints` | Bearer | Create endpoint |
| GET | `/api/endpoints/[slug]` | Bearer | Get endpoint |
| PATCH | `/api/endpoints/[slug]` | Bearer | Update endpoint |
| DELETE | `/api/endpoints/[slug]` | Bearer | Delete endpoint |
| POST | `/api/endpoints/claim` | Bearer | Claim a guest endpoint |

### Requests

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/requests` | Bearer | List requests (limit, since, cursor, kind=http\|email) |
| GET | `/api/requests/[id]` | Bearer | Get single request |
| GET | `/api/search/requests` | Bearer | Search requests (slug, method, kind, q, from, to) |
| GET | `/api/search/requests/count` | Bearer | Count matching requests |

### Webhooks

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| POST | `/api/send-test` | Bearer | Send test webhook (rate limit: 30/min) |
| POST | `/api/send-test-email` | Bearer | Deliver a sample email to an endpoint, body `{ "slug": "...", "tag": "..." }` with `tag` optional (rate limit: 10/min) |

### Email forwarding

Forwarding settings are owner only. The owner-only routes below answer `404` to anyone else.

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| PATCH | `/api/endpoints/[slug]` | Bearer, owner | Set `forwardUrl` and `forwardEnabled` (team members get `403`) |
| GET | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/forwarding` | Bearer, owner | Get the signing secret: `{ "secret": "whsec_..." }` |
| POST | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/forwarding` | Bearer, owner | Rotate the signing secret, returns the new one |
| POST | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/forwarding/test` | Bearer, owner | Post the newest email (or a sample) once and report the answer (rate limit: 10/min) |
| GET | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/deliveries` | Bearer, owner | Latest deliveries, `limit` 1 to 20 (default 5) |
| GET | `/api/requests/[id]/deliveries` | Bearer | Deliveries of one email with every attempt; anyone who can read the email |
| POST | `/api/requests/[id]/deliveries` | Bearer, owner | Redeliver the email; `409` when forwarding is off (rate limit: 30/min) |

## Conditional Response Rules

Endpoints can have an ordered list of conditional response rules. Each rule has match conditions and its own response (status, headers, body, delay). Rules are evaluated in order, and the first match wins. If no rule matches, the default `mockResponse` is returned. If no default exists, the endpoint returns 200 OK.

### Rule Structure

```typescript
interface ResponseRule {
  id?: string;                    // Stable ID for UI reordering
  name?: string;                  // Human-readable label (max 200 chars)
  enabled?: boolean;              // Default: true
  logic?: "and" | "or";          // How conditions combine (default: "and")
  conditions: ResponseRuleCondition[];  // 1-10 conditions per rule
  response: MockResponse;         // Status, body, headers, delay
}

interface ResponseRuleCondition {
  field: "method" | "path" | "header" | "body_contains" | "body_path" | "query";
  op: "eq" | "contains" | "starts_with" | "matches" | "exists";
  value?: string;                 // Required for non-"exists" ops (max 4096 chars)
  name?: string;                  // Required for header/query conditions (max 256 chars)
  path?: string;                  // Required for body_path conditions, dot-notation (max 256 chars)
}
```

### Condition Types

| Field | Operators | Description |
|-------|-----------|-------------|
| `method` | `eq` | HTTP method (case-insensitive) |
| `path` | `eq`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `matches` | Request path after slug. `matches` uses glob patterns (`*` = segment, `**` = any) |
| `header` | `exists`, `eq`, `contains` | Header lookup by `name` (case-insensitive) |
| `body_contains` | `contains` | Substring search in raw body |
| `body_path` | `exists`, `eq`, `contains` | JSON dot-notation path (e.g. `data.object.id`, `items.0.name`) |
| `query` | `exists`, `eq` | Query parameter lookup by `name` |

### Limits

- Max 50 rules per endpoint
- Max 10 conditions per rule
- Glob patterns max 500 chars
- Body JSON parsing is lazy: only triggered when a `body_path` condition exists

### SDK Usage

```typescript
// Create endpoint with conditional rules
const endpoint = await client.endpoints.create({
  name: "multi-provider",
  responseRules: [
    {
      name: "Stripe invoices",
      logic: "and",
      conditions: [
        { field: "header", op: "exists", name: "stripe-signature" },
        { field: "body_path", op: "eq", path: "type", value: "invoice.paid" },
      ],
      response: { status: 200, body: '{"received": true}', headers: { "content-type": "application/json" } },
    },
    {
      name: "GitHub pushes",
      conditions: [
        { field: "header", op: "eq", name: "x-github-event", value: "push" },
      ],
      response: { status: 202, body: "accepted", headers: {} },
    },
    {
      name: "Any PUT or PATCH",
      logic: "or",
      conditions: [
        { field: "method", op: "eq", value: "PUT" },
        { field: "method", op: "eq", value: "PATCH" },
      ],
      response: { status: 204, body: "", headers: {} },
    },
  ],
  mockResponse: { status: 200, body: "ok", headers: {} }, // default fallback
});

// Update rules on existing endpoint
await client.endpoints.update("my-slug", {
  responseRules: [/* new rules */],
});

// Clear all rules
await client.endpoints.update("my-slug", {
  responseRules: null,
});
```

### MCP Usage

The `create_endpoint` and `update_endpoint` MCP tools accept `responseRules` with the same schema. Pass `responseRules: null` to clear rules.

### Dashboard

The endpoint settings dialog includes a visual rule editor with:
- Drag-to-reorder rules (first match wins)
- Enable/disable toggle per rule
- AND/OR logic selector
- Condition builder with field-aware operator and input dropdowns
- Per-rule response configuration (status, headers, body, delay)
- Default response section below rules

### Evaluation Flow

1. Webhook arrives at receiver
2. `capture_webhook()` returns rules + default mock from Postgres
3. Rust receiver evaluates rules in order (first match wins)
4. If no rule matches, default `mockResponse` is used
5. If no default exists, returns 200 OK

---

## Webhook Capture Details

Any HTTP method, content type, and body up to 1 MB is accepted at `https://go.webhooks.cc/w/<slug>`.

Captured data per request:
- HTTP method
- Path (after slug)
- All headers (proxy headers filtered)
- Body (text)
- Query parameters
- Content-Type
- Client IP
- Received timestamp
- Body size in bytes

Mock responses can return custom status codes (100-599), headers, body, and an optional delay (0-30 seconds). Conditional response rules allow different responses based on request properties (method, path, headers, body content, JSON paths, query params). The first matching rule wins, with fallback to the default mock response.

When the database has a transient problem, the receiver answers `503` with `Retry-After: 5` so senders retry. Permanent errors fail open with `200 OK`.

---

## Email Capture

Docs: https://webhooks.cc/docs/email-capture

Every endpoint that belongs to an account receives email at `<slug>@mailhooks.cc`, on every plan, including endpoints shared with a team. Add a tag after a plus sign (`<slug>+signup@mailhooks.cc`) to tell test runs or flows apart: tagged mail lands on the same endpoint and the tag is kept on the email. The slug is not case sensitive; the tag is kept exactly as written. Guest endpoints (created without an account) receive no email, because anyone who knows a guest slug can read what it captured. The address is in each endpoint's `emailAddress` field (`null` for guest endpoints).

An email is stored as an ordinary request, in the same list as webhooks:

- `kind`: `"email"` (`"http"` for everything else)
- `method`: `"EMAIL"`
- `path`: the recipient address
- `body`: the original message, or only its headers when the message is over 1 MB
- `headers`: the message headers
- `contentType`: `message/rfc822`
- `ip`: the sending mail server's IP address
- `email`: the parsed message (below)

```typescript
// The `email` field of GET /api/requests/{id}, the request list routes, and search results
interface EmailCapture {
  subject: string | null;
  from: EmailAddress[];
  to: EmailAddress[];
  cc: EmailAddress[];
  replyTo: EmailAddress[];
  sender: EmailAddress[];
  date: string | null;             // the Date header as RFC 3339
  messageId: string | null;
  inReplyTo: string[];
  tag: string | null;              // the +tag of the address
  text: string | null;             // up to 256 KB
  html: string | null;             // up to 256 KB
  textFromHtml: boolean;           // no text part, so text was derived from the HTML
  attachments: {                   // contents are not kept
    filename: string | null;
    contentType: string;
    size: number;
    contentId: string | null;
    inline: boolean;
  }[];
  auth: {                          // sender checks run when the message arrived
    spf: { result: string; domain: string | null } | null;
    dkim: { result: string; domain: string | null; selector: string | null }[];
    dmarc: { result: string; domain: string | null; policy: string | null; reason: string | null } | null;
    iprev: { result: string; ptr: string | null } | null;   // reverse DNS
    authenticationResults: string | null;
    error: string | null;          // set when the checks could not run
  } | null;
  smtp: {
    clientIp: string | null;
    clientRdns: string | null;
    helo: string | null;
    tls: { version: string | null; cipher: string | null } | null;
    envelopeFrom: string | null;
    envelopeTo: string[];
    size: number | null;           // whole message in bytes
    test: boolean;                 // the dashboard's "Send test email" sample
  } | null;
  parseError: boolean;             // unparseable; the original is still in body
  truncated: {
    raw: boolean;                  // over 1 MB, body holds the headers only
    text: boolean;
    html: boolean;
    headers: boolean;
    addresses: boolean;
    attachments: boolean;
  };
}

interface EmailAddress {
  name: string | null;
  address: string | null;
}
```

Check results are strings such as `pass`, `fail`, `softfail`, `neutral`, `none`, `temperror` and `permerror`. Failing a check does not stop a message from being captured.

Finding emails through the API:

- `GET /api/endpoints/<slug>/requests?kind=email` (also on `/requests/paginated`) and `GET /api/search/requests?kind=email` (or `method=EMAIL`) return only emails; `kind=http` only webhooks.
- The SSE stream (`/api/stream/<slug>`) sends emails as `request` events with `kind: "email"` and `method: "EMAIL"`, without `email`, and names the request id `_id`. Fetch the request by that id for the parsed message.
- `POST /api/send-test-email` with `{ "slug": "<slug>" }` delivers a sample message with a six-digit code and a link; add `"tag": "<tag>"` to send it to `<slug>+<tag>@mailhooks.cc`. It counts as one request and does not travel over SMTP, so no sender checks run on it.
- In the SDK: `client.emails` (see TypeScript SDK Reference above).

Limits and SMTP replies:

- An email counts as one request against the same quota as webhooks, once per endpoint it is addressed to. A sender's retry after a temporary failure is captured once; sending the same message again on purpose captures it again.
- Messages up to 10 MB, up to 20 recipients per message.
- `250` captured; `550 5.1.1` no endpoint with that slug; `550 5.7.1` guest endpoint; `552 5.2.2` request quota used up; `552 5.3.4` message over 10 MB; `452` for recipients past the 20th; `451` temporary problem, the sender retries.
- Emails follow the plan's retention, like HTTP requests.
- `mailhooks.cc` only receives. It never sends mail, replies, or bounces of its own.
- Notification URLs fire for emails too, with `"method": "EMAIL"` and the recipient address as `path`.

---

## Email Forwarding

Docs: https://webhooks.cc/docs/forwarding

Forwarding posts every email an endpoint captures to your own URL as parsed JSON, usually within a second or two. HTTP requests are not forwarded. Only the endpoint's owner can configure it. It is available on every plan and does not use request quota (each email already counted once when it arrived).

### Set up

```bash
# Save the URL and turn forwarding on (the first URL creates the signing secret)
curl -X PATCH https://webhooks.cc/api/endpoints/<slug> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer whcc_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"forwardUrl": "https://example.com/hooks/email", "forwardEnabled": true}'

# Read the signing secret for your handler
curl https://webhooks.cc/api/endpoints/<slug>/forwarding \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer whcc_..."
# {"secret": "whsec_..."}

# Post the newest email (or a sample) once and see what your server answered
curl -X POST https://webhooks.cc/api/endpoints/<slug>/forwarding/test \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer whcc_..."
# {"status": 200, "durationMs": 182, "excerpt": "ok", "error": null, "delivered": true, "sample": false}
```

`forwardEnabled: true` needs a `forwardUrl`. Saving a URL before turning forwarding on lets you set up the handler and send a test delivery first. Endpoint objects carry `forwardEnabled`, `hasForwardSecret` and (for the owner only) `forwardUrl`.

### The request

```http
POST /hooks/email HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: webhooks.cc (+https://webhooks.cc/docs/forwarding)
webhook-id: msg_0b9e5f3a6c1d4f7e9a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b
webhook-timestamp: 1791450602
webhook-signature: v1,K5oZfzN95Z9UVu1EsfQmfVNQhnkZ2pj9o9NDN/H/pI4=
```

The body is the same JSON the dashboard's JSON tab shows for the email:

```typescript
interface ForwardedEmail {
  type: "email.received";
  timestamp: string;               // ISO 8601, when the email arrived; the same on every copy
  data: {
    id: string;                    // the request id; webhook-id is "msg_" + this id without dashes
    endpoint: { slug: string; name: string | null };
    receivedAt: string;            // ISO 8601
    address: string;               // the address it arrived at, tag included
    tag: string | null;
    subject: string | null;
    from: EmailAddress | null;     // the first From address
    to: EmailAddress[];
    cc: EmailAddress[];
    replyTo: EmailAddress[];
    date: string | null;
    messageId: string | null;
    inReplyTo: string[];
    text: string | null;           // up to 256 KB; derived from the HTML when there is no text part
    html: string | null;           // up to 256 KB
    codes?: string[];              // one-time codes; left out when showEmailExtracts is false
    links?: { url: string; text: string | null }[];  // links worth clicking; same rule
    attachments: {                 // contents are not kept, so not forwarded
      filename: string | null;
      contentType: string;
      size: number;
      contentId: string | null;
      inline: boolean;
    }[];
    auth: { spf: string | null; dkim: string | null; dmarc: string | null; tls: string | null };
    headers: Record<string, string>;  // lowercase names, repeated headers joined with "\n"
    size: number;                  // whole message in bytes
    truncated: { text: boolean; html: boolean };
    test: boolean;                 // the "Send test email" sample, or the sample a test delivery sends
  };
}
```

### Verify the signature (Standard Webhooks)

The signature is `v1,` followed by the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `${webhook-id}.${webhook-timestamp}.${rawBody}`. The key is the base64 after the `whsec_` prefix of the secret, decoded. `webhook-signature` may hold several space-separated signatures; accept the request when any matches. Verify against the raw body before parsing JSON, compare in constant time, and reject a `webhook-timestamp` more than 300 seconds from your clock.

With the SDK, `verifyForwardedEmail` checks the headers, the timestamp (300 seconds by default) and the signature, and returns the typed event. It takes a Fetch `Headers`, a plain object or name and value pairs, and the raw body as a string, `Uint8Array` or `ArrayBuffer`:

```typescript
import { verifyForwardedEmail, WebhookVerificationError } from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  try {
    const event = await verifyForwardedEmail(await request.text(), request.headers, process.env.FORWARD_SECRET!);
    // event.type === "email.received"; event.data is typed
    return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof WebhookVerificationError) {
      return new Response(error.message, { status: error.code === "invalid_payload" ? 400 : 401 });
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

(`verifyStandardWebhookSignature(body, headers, secret)` also accepts a Fetch `Headers` now, but checks the signature only, not the timestamp.)

In Node without dependencies:

```typescript
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

function verify(rawBody: string, headers: Record<string, string>, secret: string): boolean {
  const id = headers["webhook-id"];
  const timestamp = headers["webhook-timestamp"];
  if (!id || !timestamp || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(timestamp)) > 300) return false;
  const key = Buffer.from(secret.replace(/^whsec_/, ""), "base64");
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", key).update(`${id}.${timestamp}.${rawBody}`).digest();
  return (headers["webhook-signature"] ?? "").split(" ").some((part) => {
    const given = Buffer.from(part.replace(/^v1,/, ""), "base64");
    return given.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(given, expected);
  });
}
```

The official Standard Webhooks libraries (https://github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks) verify these headers too. Rotating the secret (`POST /api/endpoints/<slug>/forwarding`) signs every delivery from then on with the new one, retries included.

### Delivery and retries

- Any `2xx` answer accepts a delivery. Redirects are not followed and count as failures. Your server has 15 seconds to answer.
- A failed delivery is retried after 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 3 hours, 6 hours and 12 hours (about a day in all), then marked failed.
- Every copy of one email has the same `webhook-id`, so a handler can skip repeats. Delivery is at least once, in no guaranteed order.
- A retry goes to the URL and secret saved at that moment. Turning forwarding off marks deliveries still waiting as failed.
- `POST /api/requests/<id>/deliveries` queues a redelivery with the current settings (forwarding must be on).

Delivery history (`GET /api/requests/<id>/deliveries`, newest first, up to 20):

```typescript
interface Delivery {
  id: string;
  requestId: string;
  status: "pending" | "succeeded" | "failed";
  attempts: number;
  createdAt: number;               // Unix ms
  finishedAt: number | null;
  nextAttemptAt: number | null;    // set while pending
  lastStatus: number | null;
  lastError: string | null;
  attemptLog: {                    // newest first
    attemptedAt: number;
    status: number | null;         // null when no answer arrived
    durationMs: number;
    error: string | null;
    responseExcerpt: string | null; // start of the response body, up to 1 KB
  }[];
}
```

`GET /api/endpoints/<slug>/deliveries` returns the endpoint's latest deliveries in a shorter form: `id`, `requestId`, `status`, `attempts`, `createdAt`, `lastStatus`, `lastError` and the email's `subject`.

### Limits

- The URL must be `https` on a public host name, at most 2048 characters: no IP addresses, `localhost`, private networks, credentials in the URL, or mail, database and other internal ports.
- On webhooks.cc, requests come from Cloudflare's network, not a fixed address (a self-hosted copy without the notify proxy sends from its own server). Do not allowlist IPs; check the signature.
- An email whose JSON would be larger than 10 MB is not forwarded.
- Deliveries are kept as long as the email itself.

## Rate Limits

- Endpoint creation: 30 per 10 minutes
- Send test: 30 per minute
- Send test email: 10 per minute
- Forwarding test delivery: 10 per minute
- Redeliver a forwarded email: 30 per minute
- Search: 60 per 10 minutes
- Search count: 120 per 10 minutes
- Guest endpoint creation: 20 per 10 minutes per IP
- Device auth: 10 per minute per IP

## Data Retention

- **Free plan**: 7 days
- **Pro plan**: 31 days
- **Team-billed requests** (endpoints shared with an active team): 31 days, whatever the owner's plan
- Ephemeral endpoints: 12 hours, max 25 requests
- Emails and their forwarding deliveries follow the same retention as HTTP requests
